title: Nextcloud Activity Daily Event Volume
dataSources: Proxmox node/VM metrics (`proxmox:metric`), Docker container stats (`docker:stats`), Synology/TrueNAS (`synology:disk`, `truenas:pool`), Raspberry Pi host metrics, UPS status via NUT (`nut:ups`).
app: Proxmox / Docker / Portainer, Synology/TrueNAS, Raspberry Pi, and UPS (NUT) metrics via the Splunk Universal Forwarder, collectd/telegraf, and HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=nextcloud:activity
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count as events, dc(user_id) as distinct_entities by _time
| sort - _time
description: Counts how many Nextcloud activity events land each day and how many distinct user values are represented.
value: Daily volume is the fastest way to spot a dead feed, a sudden burst, or a workflow that quietly changed.
implementation: Ingest Nextcloud activity records into `index=personal`; schedule daily and compare count and distinct user values against your normal baseline.
visualization: Column chart of daily event count with a line for distinct entities.
grandmaExplanation: It quietly how much Nextcloud activity activity showed up each day so you can see if the feed went quiet or suddenly got busy.
